newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria plans second stock exchange - papers.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria plans second stock exchange - papers.

text.p: Nigeria plans a second stock exchange for the new capital Abuja which will be independent of the current stock exchange in the commercial capital Lagos, local newspapers reported on Wednesday.

The newspapers said finance minister Anthony Ani had approved the establishment of a stock exchange in the administrative capital, as recommended by a panel set up to investigate Nigeria's capital markets.
"As part of the capital market reforms a decision has been taken to break the monopoly of the Nigerian Stock Exchange," Ani was quoted as saying by the independent Thisday newspaper.

The Nigerian Stock Exchange, which was set up in 1961, has market capitalisation of over 367 billion naira ($4.4 billion). It has branches in most large cities in Nigeria. Trade is slow and daily turnover is usually well below one tenth of one percent of market capitalisation.

Local business analysts say that what the stock exchange really needs to take off is the privatisation of the oil industry and inefficient state-run utilities. But so far the government has been reluctant to do so.

Since coming to power during political turmoil in 1993, General Sani Abacha's military government has moved as many functions of the state as possible to Abuja and away from Lagos, a hotbed of opposition to his rule.
